claims.hypothesis: Simple optical-NIR/MIR colour cuts select fast-quenching galaxies at z~2
claims.experiment: Model colours from CIGALE, then test on the COSMOS2020 catalog against photo-z, sSFR and spectroscopic redshifts
claims.result: Galaxies with z~2 and low sSFR are selected; 57 of 359 gri galaxies pass i[3.6][4.5]
claims.finding: The colour criteria select z~2 fast-quenching galaxy candidates

evidence.quote: Galaxies with photometric and/or spectroscopic redshifts $z\sim2$ and low specific star formation rates are successfully selected using these colors.

claims.hypothesis: The selected galaxies are quiescent rather than dusty star-forming
claims.experiment: 24 micron stacking and ALMA limits on spectroscopic objects, compared with SED-fit sSFR
claims.result: No stacked 24 micron detection above 2 sigma; ALMA SFR limits <~100 Msun/yr; but over half have SED-fit sSFR >1e-10 and iJH is contaminated by dusty SFGs
claims.finding: The i[3.6][4.5] criterion plausibly selects galaxies below the main sequence; iJH is more contaminated

evidence.loc: Completeness and purity of the selection method
evidence.quote: at least, our color criteria plausibly select the galaxies under the star-formation main sequence.

evidence.loc: Completeness and purity of the selection method
evidence.quote: contaminated by dusty SFGs.

claims.hypothesis: Spectroscopically confirmed galaxies that pass the criteria are massive quiescent galaxies
claims.experiment: Spectra, morphologies and ALMA/24 micron limits of three confirmed objects
claims.result: Dn(4000) ~1.4, no emission lines, no ALMA or 24 micron detection
claims.finding: They are well characterized as massive quiescent galaxies at z~2

evidence.quote: From these above, all the spectroscopically confirmed objects satisfying our color criteria are well characterized as massive quiescent galaxies at $z\sim2$

claims.hypothesis: Massive galaxies near the main sequence at z=3-4 are the progenitors
claims.experiment: Compare comoving number densities of selected galaxies with SMGs and massive galaxies at z=3-4.5
claims.result: 4 (2) percent of massive z=3-4.5 galaxies quenching immediately would explain the density
claims.finding: Progenitors are massive galaxies not far above the main sequence, not extreme starbursts

evidence.quote: The number density of these fast-quenching galaxy candidates at $z\sim2$ suggests that massive galaxies not so far above the star-formation main sequence at $z=3-4$ should be their progenitors.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA enters only as two flux limits with no reduction details, so the SFR limits cannot be checked
Only three spectroscopic galaxies test the selection, and only one comes from earlier quiescent samples
Over half of the colour-selected galaxies have SED-fit sSFR >1e-10, so purity is weakly constrained
Number-density progenitor argument rests on a rough conservative estimate
